problem: GENIE could retrieve canonical Experience only when the caller already knew a structural key, so a problem-only cross-context request could not discover important History reachable through indirect evidence references.

decision.decision_summary: Add one read-only literal-problem History lookup beside the unchanged exact-key API. Select only canonical Experience by its problem phrase, then follow only its explicit repository JSON references with in-place byte resolution and SHA enforcement.
decision.retrieval_contribution: The real OOM query independently recovered July evidence and used it to reject heap-only retry and coverage-reducing exclusions.

action.action_summary: Extended the existing canonical retrieval service and its existing verifier without creating an index, semantic/vector/RAG system, or copying reports into Experience.

evidence.evidence_detail: Problem-only OOM query found canonical Experience and resolved the 2026-07-28 source report with exact SHA and original 8GB caveat; all 11 regressions passed before capture at 113 Experiences and after capture at 114.

cause.root_cause_summary: The July History existed and a later canonical Experience already referenced it indirectly, but exact-key selection and evidence resolution were separate operations with no problem-only bridge. Repository inventory was metadata-only and older than the History.

lesson: Cross-context recall does not require semantic infrastructure when canonical Experience already names the problem and preserves explicit provenance: literal selection plus strict reference-chain resolution can recover original History without duplicating it.
